steps.title: Errors during execution
steps.content: An exception is an event that interrupts normal program flow, such as dividing by zero, opening a missing file or converting invalid input. Handling exceptions lets a program respond safely.
steps.example: Converting the text 'abc' to an integer raises a ValueError in Python.

steps.title: Choose a specific exception
steps.prompt: Which Python exception is raised by int('hello')?
steps.explanation: The argument is a string, but it does not contain a valid integer representation, so int() raises ValueError.

steps.title: Use try and except
steps.content: Place risky code in try. Add an except block for the specific exception you can handle. Avoid catching every exception unless you can safely recover.
steps.example: try: age = int(text)\nexcept ValueError: print('Enter a whole number')
steps.tip: Catch the narrowest meaningful exception so unexpected bugs are not hidden.

steps.title: Understand finally
steps.prompt: In Python, when does a finally block run?
options: Only when there is no exception
After try/except whether an exception occurs or not
steps.explanation: finally runs as control leaves the try statement, whether or not an exception occurred.

steps.title: Raise and clean up
steps.content: Use raise to signal an invalid condition. Use finally or a context manager to release resources. In Python, with open(...) automatically closes a file even if an exception occurs.
steps.example: if quantity < 0: raise ValueError('Quantity cannot be negative')

questions.prompt: Which block contains code that may raise an exception?
questions.explanation: The try block contains code that may fail.

questions.prompt: Which exception commonly occurs when accessing a missing dictionary key with d[key]?
questions.explanation: A missing dictionary key raises KeyError.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of except?
questions.explanation: except runs when an exception matching its handler is raised.

questions.prompt: Why is catching Exception broadly risky?
options: It may hide unexpected programming errors
questions.explanation: A broad catch can mask bugs that should be fixed rather than silently handled.
